observable: the User-Agent request header, on navigation and on subresource requests

evidence.note: browser process writes it on navigations via ComputeUserAgentValue, which falls back to GetContentClient()->browser()->GetUserAgent()
renderer writes it on subresource requests from FrameLoader::UserAgent — the same cached browser value navigator.userAgent reads
network service applies StaticHttpUserAgentSettings::GetUserAgent with SetHeaderIfMissing as a last-resort default, from NetworkContextParams.user_agent set at chrome_content_browser_client.cc:6963

evidence.source: own capture (resources/fingerprints/raw/apple-m4-max-20260907T033252Z.json): probes['headers.echo'].value.headers: User-Agent identical to probes['navigator.scalars'].value.userAgent

notes: Three writers across three processes, but only one origin: all of them read embedder_support::GetUserAgent(). Unlike Device-Memory there is no independent recomputation, so this is a waypoint chain rather than a duplication. It still matters which is patched: the browser writes the navigation header before any renderer exists, so a Blink-side change cannot cover the first request.

evidence.note: ComputeAcceptLanguage runs the pref through ReduceAcceptLanguageUtils::GetLanguagesWithMaxCount, then net::HttpUtil::ExpandLanguageList and GenerateAcceptLanguageHeader — a different transform from the one the renderer applies to the same pref
written into NetworkContextParams.accept_language, i.e. it lives in the network service, not the renderer
AddExtraHeaders applies it with SetHeaderIfMissing from HttpUserAgentSettings; net/url_request/static_http_user_agent_settings.cc:18 is the accessor
the q-value form on the wire versus the bare array in JavaScript — the two shapes differ because the transforms differ

notes: The second confirmed multi-process duplication in this shard, and the one most likely to be missed because both halves look like 'the language setting'. navigator.languages is produced in the renderer from RendererPreferences (renderer_preferences_util.cc:193); this header is produced in the network service from NetworkContextParams (profile_network_context_service.cc:1356). Same pref, two functions, two processes, two output shapes. Patch one and a server sees a header that contradicts JavaScript, exactly as with Device-Memory. Additional wrinkle: ReduceAcceptLanguageUtils can persist a per-origin reduced language, so the header is not necessarily constant across origins — a V3 run should sample more than one origin.

observable: the Sec-CH-UA-* headers on a fetch() issued from a dedicated Worker, SharedWorker or ServiceWorker, compared against the same fetch from the main thread

evidence.note: WorkerFetchContext::PopulateResourceRequestBeforeCacheAccess does mixed-content upgrade and top-frame-origin only; there is no AddClientHintsIfNecessary and no client-hints code anywhere in the file

evidence.source: grep of every kUA* client-hint constant across the tree at 152.0.7977.82 returns writers only in content/browser/client_hints/client_hints.cc and third_party/blink/renderer/core/loader/frame_fetch_context.cc
evidence.note: so on the evidence available no renderer path attaches UA client hints to worker-initiated requests

notes: Escalated rather than closed. What is unresolved: whether a worker-initiated fetch reaches the wire with no Sec-CH-UA at all, or picks the headers up on some path outside these two files (a ServiceWorker respondWith replaying a main-thread request, or a network-service default). It matters in both directions — if hints are absent that is stock behaviour and needs no patch, but the header rows in this shard cannot claim full coverage until it is known; if some third path exists it is an emitter this map is missing. What would settle it: one T0 capture that fetches the headers.echo endpoint from the main thread, a dedicated Worker and a ServiceWorker in the same session and diffs the three header sets. That probe does not exist in the current collector.

observable: the browser brand entry in navigator.userAgentData.brands and the Sec-CH-UA header

evidence.note: brand = version_info::GetProductName() is compiled in only under #if !BUILDFLAG(CHROMIUM_BRANDING); a Chromium-branded build therefore produces a brand list with no browser entry
three entries — Chromium, Not?A_Brand, Google Chrome — so the browser entry is present on a real Chrome and its absence is itself the tell

notes: Chrome branding normally needs src-internal, which is not public, and that is why forks ship Chromium-branded. It does not follow that the brand list must be wrong: the guard suppresses one assignment, and a patch supplying the brand reaches every consumer. Distinct from the product name shown in chrome://version, which is not page-readable.

observable: the 'Headless' token in navigator.userAgent and in the User-Agent header
verdict_reason: A real Chrome never emits this token. It is inserted purely because the browser was launched with --headless, which is a fact about how we run rather than about the device being claimed.

evidence.note: GetUserAgentInternal() inserts "Headless" at the front of the product token when the --headless switch is present, upstream of every consumer of the UA string
an earlier collector ran under headless Chrome and the token appeared in the captured UA, which is how that capture was identified as unusable

notes: Single insertion point upstream of every consumer, so one patch covers the UA string and every header derived from it.
